stories.headline: China's $900 Billion Chip Stock Boom Masks Deepening Property Crisis
stories.thesis: Chinese chip stocks surged $900 billion as IPOs and Huawei expansion drive a historic semiconductor rally — but a leading property developer reports widening losses, and falling oil imports signal industrial demand destruction beneath the tech rally.

stories.headline: US Plans Cuts to NATO Rapid Response Force as Deep-Sea Cable Sabotage Expands
stories.thesis: The US is cutting NATO's rapid response force — the unit designed for hybrid threats — while suspected sabotage triggers NATO's first-ever collective response. Strategic posture and operational reality are diverging.

stories.headline: Tech Groups Monetise AI Hype by Selling Volatility as SpaceX, Broadcom Signal Diverging AI Paths
stories.thesis: Tech groups have found a new way to profit from AI mania — selling volatility products to investors chasing AI exposure. Meanwhile Goldman Sachs expects SpaceX's AI revenue to increase 100-fold by 2030, even as Broadcom's $285bn rout raises questions about AI semiconductor demand concentration.

stories.headline: Bitcoin Tumbles After Strategy Sale Unnerves Crypto Traders
stories.thesis: Bitcoin dropped sharply after Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) sold a significant position, spooking crypto markets. The selloff tests the thesis that crypto infrastructure is transitioning from speculation to machine-to-machine capital rails.

stories.headline: India Rate-Hike Bets Build as Pricey Oil and Weak Rupee Stoke Inflation Risks
stories.thesis: India's central bank faces growing pressure to hike rates as oil prices strain import costs and the rupee weakens. A little-known Indian stock's 530% rally shows hidden AI winners emerging in India's market as capital rotates from China.

stories.headline: Morgan Stanley Warns Fed Is Discounting Iran War in Rate Calculus — Transitory Framing at Risk
stories.thesis: Morgan Stanley's research finds the Fed is treating the Iran war as a transitory supply shock in its rate decision framework. If energy costs persist, the 'transitory' framing will force a hard repricing of rate expectations across the curve.
